settings.repere: Intertitre · How long does one bag of cat litter la…
settings.text: How long does one bag of cat litter last?

settings.repere: Paragraphe · In a household with a single cat, a 6l…
settings.text: In a household with a single cat, a 6lb bag of litter lasts about a month before needing to be replaced. However, there are some factors that can affect consumption such as the size of the cat's litter box and how often it gets scooped and replaced. Our silica gel crystals are extremely absorbent, so you'll likely need less of it to do the same job.

settings.repere: Intertitre · How many inches of cat litter goes int…
settings.text: How many inches of cat litter goes into the litter box?

settings.repere: Paragraphe · Litter boxes using PrettyLitter should…
settings.text: Litter boxes using PrettyLitter should have two inches of depth to them, so the correct amount of kitty litter will vary on the size of the litter box. With PrettyLitter's absorbent silica-gel crystal formula, one fill should last an entire month for one medium-sized cat.

settings.repere: Intertitre · Can you buy PrettyLitter without a sub…
settings.text: Can you buy PrettyLitter without a subscription?

settings.repere: Paragraphe · Yes. You can buy PrettyLitter as a one…
settings.text: Yes. You can buy PrettyLitter as a one-time purchase. However, a subscription offers added convenience, automatic delivery, and savings. You can also cancel anytime.

settings.repere: Intertitre · What do the PrettyLitter colors indica…
settings.text: What do the PrettyLitter colors indicate?

settings.repere: Paragraphe · PrettyLitter changes color based on yo…
settings.text: PrettyLitter changes color based on your cat’s urine pH. Yellow/olive green is typical, while blue may indicate alkaline urine, orange indicates acidic urine, and red indicates visible blood. Color changes can help monitor your cat’s health but cannot diagnose medical conditions. Contact your veterinarian if you notice unusual colors.

settings.repere: Intertitre · Is PrettyLitter safe for my cat?
settings.text: Is PrettyLitter safe for my cat?

settings.repere: Paragraphe · Yes. PrettyLitter is made with amorpho…
settings.text:
Yes. PrettyLitter is made with amorphous silica gel — a non-toxic, pet-safe material. It's important to note that not all silica is the same: amorphous silica (the kind used in PrettyLitter) is safe, while crystalline silica (found in some clay litters) can be harmful when inhaled over time. And those "Do not eat" labels you see on silica packets? They signal a choking hazard, not toxicity.

Safety is backed by rigorous third-party testing for both respiratory and digestive safety, plus ongoing toxicologist review of all materials.

settings.repere: Intertitre · Does PrettyLitter clump?
settings.text: Does PrettyLitter clump?

settings.repere: Paragraphe · PrettyLitter offers both Original Non-…
settings.text: PrettyLitter offers both Original Non-Clumping and Clumping formulas. Original PrettyLitter absorbs urine without forming clumps, while PrettyLitter Clumping forms scoopable clumps for easier cleanup.

settings.repere: Intertitre · What are the ingredients of PrettyLitt…
settings.text: What are the ingredients of PrettyLitter?

settings.repere: Paragraphe · PrettyLitter is made with super-absorb…
settings.text: PrettyLitter is made with super-absorbent silica gel crystals designed to absorb urine and help control odor. The litter also contains a health-monitoring formula that can help indicate changes in urine pH and visible blood.

settings.repere: Intertitre · Is PrettyLitter compatible with the Li…
settings.text: Is PrettyLitter compatible with the Litter-Robot?

settings.repere: Paragraphe · Non-clumping PrettyLitter is compatibl…
settings.text:
Non-clumping PrettyLitter is compatible with most self-cleaning, automated litter boxes. Clumping PrettyLitter is not recommended for automated litter boxes.

Many customers love using our litter in the Litter Robot 3 and earlier generations of the Litter Robot, along with other manufacturer’s models. PrettyLitter is not ideal for the Litter Robot 4, because the machine’s sensors do not detect our light-colored litter.

If you have questions about a specific make and model, we recommend reaching out to the manufacturer to ensure compatibility.
